title-group.article-title: Markers of endothelial activation and progression of white matter hyperintensities

sec.title: Introduction
sec.p: Cerebral small vessel disease is poorly understood at the molecular level. Endothelial activation may play a causal role in white matter hyperintensities.

sec.title: Materials and Methods
sec.p: We performed magnetic resonance imaging of 296 community subjects at baseline and at three- and six-year follow-up. Plasma intercellular adhesion molecule was quantified by ELISA.
Statistical analysis used logistic regression adjusted for age and sex.

sec.title: Statistical Methods
sec.p: Odds ratios were estimated with ninety-five percent confidence intervals using Stata version fourteen.

sec.title: Results
sec.p: Intercellular adhesion molecule levels were associated with white matter hyperintensity progression at three and six years. The odds ratio at three years was 1.007 per nanogram per millilitre.

sec.title: Discussion
sec.p: The prospective design supports a causal role for endothelial activation in cerebral small vessel disease pathogenesis. Other coagulation markers were not associated with progression.
